key_factors: Polling average shows Talarico up ~3 in a state with a 6-point Republican lean
Paxton's heavy liabilities: $27M in outside opposition spending and a divisive primary win over Cornyn
Talarico's massive fundraising edge ($146M raised, $9.9M on hand)
Prediction markets price Talarico near 70% despite the tossup ratings
model.rationale: The polling average (~+2.9 Talarico), a favorable midterm environment, Paxton's unusually high unfavorables reflected in outside spending, and Talarico's overwhelming financial advantage all point the same direction, and markets agree at roughly 70%. The state's Republican lean and a couple of late polls showing Paxton narrowly ahead keep this short of Likely D.
model.watch: Turnout composition in a record early-vote electorate, especially suburban and young voters, could shift the margin several points either way.
notes: Open seat: John Cornyn (R) is not on the ballot.

overview: Texas's open Senate seat has become one of the closest races of the cycle. State Senator James Talarico, a prolific fundraiser, faces Attorney General Ken Paxton, who ousted Senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary. Recent polls mostly show Talarico ahead by one to six points, though a few put Paxton narrowly on top, and the polling average sits near three points for the Democrat. Expert raters split between Tossup and Lean D, and prediction markets price Talarico around 70 percent. Paxton carries significant baggage, reflected in tens of millions of outside spending against him, while Talarico has outraised him by a wide margin. Still, Texas's Republican lean means a narrow Democratic edge in polls does not guarantee a win. Early voting has topped six million ballots, and the final margin will hinge on turnout in the closing days.
